## Tiny Table Examples

```{=typst}
// if not created by yaml
#outline(
  title: [List of Figures],
  target: figure.where(kind: "quarto-float-fig")
)

#outline(
  title: [List of Tables],
  target: figure.where(kind: "quarto-float-tbl")
)
```

#set page(flipped: true)
```

### TT Eg1

```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg1
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg1"

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr)
mtcars %>% head() %>% tt(align = 'left')
print("First Few Rows of mtcars")
```

Table @tbl-TT-Eg1 for examples of TinyTable outputs with different styles and captions.

### TT Eg14
```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg14
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg14"
#| tbl-subcap:
#|  - "TT-Eg14A"
#|  - "TT-Eg14B"
#| cap-location: bottom

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, gt)
dat <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Sales", "Conversion", "Growth", "Efficiency"),
  Value = c(75, 45, 92, 38),
  Percentage = c(0.75, 0.45, 0.92, 0.38)
)

tt(dat) |>  plot_tt(    j = 2,    fun = "bar",    data = as.list(dat$Value),    color = "darkorange"  ) |>  plot_tt(    j = 3,    fun = "bar",    data = as.list(dat$Percentage),    color = c("steelblue", "lightgrey"),    xlim = c(0, 1)  )

carAvg <- mtcars %>%  group_by(gear) %>%  summarise(across(c(mpg, disp, hp), mean, .names = "avg_{col}"))

#carAvg %>% gt()

carAvg %>%  tt() |>  plot_tt(    j = 2,    fun = "bar",    data = as.list(carAvg$avg_mpg),    color = "darkorange"  ) |>  plot_tt(    j = 3,    fun = "bar",    data = as.list(carAvg$avg_disp),    color = c("steelblue", "lightgrey"),    xlim = c(0, 1)  ) |>  plot_tt(    j = 4,    fun = "bar",    data = as.list(carAvg$avg_hp),    color = c("steelblue", "lightgrey"),    xlim = c(0, 1)  )

The first table @tbl-TT-Eg14-1 shows how to plot bar charts for the `Value` and `Percentage` columns, while the second table @tbl-TT-Eg14-2 shows how to plot bar charts for the average `mpg`, `disp`, and `hp` values grouped by the number of gears.

tmp %>%  group_by(gearGroup) %>%  sample_n(2) %>%  tt(    width = c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1),    height = 2,    caption = "Grouped by Gear",    notes = "This table shows the first 3 rows of mtcars grouped by the number of gears."  ) %>%  theme_striped()

grp %>% tt()

```

### TT Eg17
```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg17
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg17"
#| tbl-subcap:
#|  - "TT-Eg17A"
#|  - "TT-Eg17B"
#| cap-location: bottom

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, gt)

tmp <- mtcars %>%  select(mpg, cyl, gear, am) %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  arrange(gear, mpg) %>%  group_by(gear) %>%  mutate(gearGroup = paste0("Gear: ", gear, " | No. of Cars: ", n())) %>%  ungroup()

#tmp %>% group_by(gearGroup)  %>% tt(width = c(1, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1), height = 2, caption = "Grouped by Gear", notes = "This table shows the first 3 rows of mtcars grouped by the number of gears.") %>% theme_striped()

# Group labels and last row position of each group

grp <- tmp %>%
  count(gearGroup, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(start = cumsum(n) - n + 1, position = start - 1, end = cumsum(n) + 1)

#grp
group_labels1 <- as.list(setNames(grp$end, grp$gearGroup))
group_labels2 <- as.list(setNames(grp$start, grp$gearGroup))

# Create table
tmp %>%  tt() %>%  group_tt(i = group_labels1) %>%  subset(select = -gearGroup) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  style_tt(i = "groupi", align = "l", color = "red", line = "b") %>%  theme_striped()

tmp %>%  tt() %>%  group_tt(i = group_labels2) %>%  subset(select = -gearGroup) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  style_tt(i = "groupi", align = "l", color = "teal", line = "b") %>%  theme_typst()
```
The tables shows how to display groups of rows in the table, while the second table shows how to display groups of rows with custom labels.
with typst unbreakable block, the table can be broken across pages if it is too long to fit on a single page. The `set block(breakable: true)` command allows the table to be broken across pages.
The first tables shows group labels at the end of each group, while the second table shows group labels at the start of each group.

### TT Eg18  : Most Popular

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-nrow: 2
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg18
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg18"
#| tbl-subcap:
#|  - "TT-Eg18A"
#|  - "TT-Eg18B"
#| cap-location: bottom

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, gt)

tmp <- mtcars %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  arrange(gear, mpg)

# Group summary
grp <- tmp %>%  group_by(gear) %>%  summarise( n = n(), avgMPG = round(mean(mpg), 2),  avgWT = round(mean(wt), 2),  .groups = "drop"  ) %>%  mutate(  label = paste0( "Gear: ", gear,  " | Cars: ", n,  " | Avg MPG: ", avgMPG,  " | Avg WT: ", avgWT   ),  end = cumsum(n), start = cumsum(n) - n +1  )

grp %>% tt() %>% style_tt(align = "c") %>% style_tt(i = 0, bold = TRUE, color = "teal", line = "b") %>%style_tt(background = "#EAF4F4") %>% theme_typst()


group_labels <- as.list(setNames(grp$end - grp$n + 1, grp$label))

# Generate tinytable
tmp %>% mutate(ser= row_number()) %>%  select(ser, Car, gear, mpg, wt, everything()) %>% tt(width = c(0.4, 2.5, rep(0.7,11)), caption='Group Heading with more details', notes='Grouped by Gear')  %>% style_tt(font_size = 8) %>%   group_tt(i = group_labels) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  style_tt(    i = "groupi",    align = "l",    color = "teal",    line = "b"  ) %>% style_tt(j = 1:2, align = "l") %>% style_tt(j = 3:5, align = "r") %>%  style_tt(j = 6:11, align = "c") %>%  theme_grid() %>% style_tt(i = 0, background = "#006D77", color = "brown", bold = TRUE)%>%  style_tt(j = 1, background = "#D9EAF7")  %>% theme_typst()

```
Width can be defined in different ways in tt

- Width can be defined as a single value, which will be applied to all columns.
    - width = 1
- Width can be defined as a vector of values, which will be applied to each column in the order they are specified.
    - width = c(120, 45, 50, 50, rep(45, ncol(tmp) - 4)),
    width = c(3, 1, 1, 1, rep(.8, ncol(tmp) - 4)),
- Width can be defined as a vector of values with names, which will be applied to each column based on the column name.



### TT Eg20 : Splitting Tables in 3 cols
```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg20
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg20"
#| tbl-subcap:
#|  - "TT-Eg20A"
#|  - "TT-Eg20B"
#| cap-location: bottom

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, gt, tidyr)

df <- mtcars %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>% select(Car, mpg, wt)

nblock <- 3
nrows <- ceiling(nrow(df) / nblock)

df_wide <- df %>%  mutate(    block = ceiling(row_number() / nrows),    row = (row_number() - 1) %% nrows + 1  ) %>%  pivot_wider(    id_cols = row,    names_from = block,    values_from = c(Car, mpg, wt),    names_glue = "{.value}_{block}"  ) %>%  select(row, Car_1, mpg_1, wt_1, Car_2, mpg_2, wt_2, Car_3, mpg_3, wt_3) %>%  select(-row)

tt(  df_wide,  caption = "Motor Cars: Three Side-by-Side Blocks",  width = rep(c(2, 1, 1), 3)) %>%  style_tt(align = "c") %>%  group_tt(j = list("GA-1" = 1:3, "GA-2" = 4:6, "GA-3" = 7:9)) %>%  theme_typst()
```

### TT Eg21 : Splitting Tables in 3 cols : Typst
```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg21
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg21"
#| cap-location: bottom
#| results: asis

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, gt, tidyr)

tmp2 <- mtcars %>%  mutate(ser = row_number()) %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  select(ser, Car, mpg, hp, wt, am)

# Convert each row into Typst table cells
cells <- apply(tmp2, 1, function(x) {
  paste0("[", x, "]", collapse = ", ")
})

typst_code <- paste0(
  "#columns(3, gutter: 10pt)[\n",
  "#set text(size: 8pt)\n",
  "#table(\n",
  "columns: (0.6fr, 1.5fr, 1fr, 1fr, 1fr, 1fr),\n",
  "inset: 3pt,\n",
  "stroke: 0.3pt + gray.lighten(60%),\n",
  "table.header([*Ser*], [*Car*], [*mpg*], [*hp*], [*wt*], [*am*]),\n",
  paste(cells, collapse = ",\n"),
  "\n)\n",
  "]"
)

cat("```{=typst}\n", typst_code, "\n```\n", sep = "")
```
Note to include results: asis in the chunk options to ensure that the Typst code is rendered correctly in the output document.



### TT Eg22 : Splitting Tables in x cols : Typst : B
```{r}
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-TT-Eg22
#| tbl-cap: "TT-Eg22"
#| cap-location: bottom
#| results: asis

pacman::p_load(tinytable, dplyr, gt, tidyr)

# User settings
ncols <- 2
font_size <- 7
gutter <- 8

# Prepare data
tmp2 <- mtcars %>%  mutate(ser = row_number()) %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  select(ser, Car, mpg, hp, wt)

# Split into consecutive groups of rows
ncols <- max(1L, min(as.integer(ncols), nrow(tmp2)))
rows_per_col <- ceiling(nrow(tmp2) / ncols)

parts <- split(tmp2, ceiling(seq_len(nrow(tmp2)) / rows_per_col))

# Convert text safely to Typst cells
typst_cell <- function(x) {
  x <- ifelse(is.na(x), "", as.character(x))
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  x <- gsub("([\\[\\]#*])", "\\\\\\1", x)
  paste0("[", x, "]")
}

# Create a Typst table for each part
make_table <- function(df) {
  headers <- paste(typst_cell(names(df)), collapse = ", ")

  rows <- apply(as.matrix(df), 1, function(x) {
    paste(typst_cell(x), collapse = ", ")
  })

  paste0(
    "table(\n",
    "columns: (0.5fr, 2fr, 0.7fr, 0.7fr, 0.7fr),\n",
    "inset: 2pt,\n",
    "stroke: 0.3pt + gray.lighten(60%),\n",
    "table.header(",
    headers,
    "),\n",
    paste(rows, collapse = ",\n"),
    "\n)"
  )
}

# Generate grid dynamically
typst_code <- paste0(
  "#{\n",
  "set text(size: ",
  font_size,
  "pt)\n",
  "grid(\n",
  "columns: (",
  paste(rep("1fr", length(parts)), collapse = ", "),
  "),\n",
  "gutter: ",
  gutter,
  "pt,\n",
  paste(vapply(parts, make_table, character(1)), collapse = ",\n"),
  "\n)\n",
  "}"
)

cat("```{=typst}\n", typst_code, "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

## Extra Tables

### TE- 1 : Highlight entire rows where mpg > 21

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TE-1
#| tbl-cap: "TE-1"
#| cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

df <- mtcars %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%
  select(Car, mpg, cyl, hp, wt, gear) %>%
  head(12)

df %>%  tt() %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg > 21),    background = "lightblue",    color = "darkblue",    bold = TRUE  )
```

### TE2. Different colours for high, medium and low mpg

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TE-2
#| tbl-cap: "TE-2"
#| cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)
df %>%  tt() %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg >= 25),    j = "mpg",    background = "lightgreen",    color = "darkgreen",    bold = TRUE  ) %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg >= 18 & df$mpg < 25),    j = "mpg",    background = "lightyellow",    color = "darkorange"  ) %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg < 18),    j = "mpg",    background = "mistyrose",    color = "darkred",    bold = TRUE  )

```

### T3. Colour cells in two different columns based on their own values

Here, mpg is coloured according to fuel efficiency, while hp is coloured according to horsepower.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TE-3
#| tbl-cap: "TE-3"
#| cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

df %>%  tt() %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg > 21),    j = "mpg",    background = "lightgreen",    color = "darkgreen"  ) %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$hp > 150),    j = "hp",    background = "lightpink",    color = "darkred",    bold = TRUE  )

```

### TE4. Highlight maximum and minimum values

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TE-4
#| tbl-cap: "TE-4"
#| cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

df %>%  tt() %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg == max(df$mpg)),    j = "mpg",    background = "lightgreen",    bold = TRUE  ) %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg == min(df$mpg)),    j = "mpg",    background = "salmon",    color = "white",    bold = TRUE  )

```

### T#5. Highlight values above and below the average

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TE-5
#| tbl-cap: "TE-5"
#| cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)

avg_mpg <- mean(df$mpg)

df %>%  tt() %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg >= avg_mpg),    j = "mpg",    background = "#D1FAE5",    color = "#065F46"  ) %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg < avg_mpg),    j = "mpg",    background = "#FEE2E2",    color = "#991B1B"  )
```

### TE6. Apply a continuous colour gradient to cells

Instead of only three categories, create a different background colour for each mpg value.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| layout-ncol: 1
#| label: tbl-TE-6
#| tbl-cap: "TE-6"
#| cap-location: bottom

library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)


df2 <- mtcars %>%  tibble::rownames_to_column("Car") %>%  select(Car, mpg, hp, wt) %>%  head(12)

pal <- scales::col_numeric(  palette = c("#FEE2E2", "#FEF08A", "#86EFAC"), domain = range(df2$mpg))

bg_colors <- pal(df2$mpg)

tab <- tt(df2)

for (k in seq_len(nrow(df2))) {
  tab <- style_tt(    tab,    i = k,    j = "mpg",    background = bg_colors[k],    color = "#111827"  )}

tab
```


```{r}
#| label: tbl-mpg-conditional
#| tbl-cap: "Conditional Formatting of Fuel Efficiency"
#| echo: false
#| message: false

df %>%   tt() %>%  style_tt(    i = which(df$mpg > 21),    j = "mpg",    background = "lightgreen",    color = "darkgreen",    bold = TRUE  ) %>%  theme_typst()
```

See @tbl-mpg-conditional for the fuel-efficiency comparison.
